title: Broadcast Archive Search & Summarization — Pilot SOW + Pricing Sketch
content:
Purpose and target customer:
This document is an internal sketch for a customer pilot: a broadcast archive search and summarization prototype for a mid-sized television network. Goal is to demonstrate rapid discovery over decades of broadcast material (video + captions), auto-generated short summaries, and time-aligned highlight snippets for editorial workflows. Not a full product SOW — working draft for scoping and pricing conversation.

Executive summary (one‑liner):
Build a 6–8 week pilot that ingests a representative slice of the customer’s broadcast archive (50–250 hours), exposes a semantic search UI with timestamped snippets, and returns concise program-level and scene-level summaries using LLM-based summarization tuned for broadcast language. Validate retrieval quality, latency, and end-to-end costs for scaling.

Workshop notes (2025-02-10 kickoff, internal):
- Attendees: Marina (SE), Ethan (ML Eng), Priya (Solutions PM), Customer: A. Reed (Head of Archives), L. Park (Editorial lead), SRE contact pending.
- Customer emphasized: fast search by concept/guest/topic, near-exact timecodes, ability to export snippet clips, redaction flagging for PII/licensing.
- Key constraints: VOD stored in S3-compatible object store, captions available for ~60% of content (legacy vendor), strict licensing logs required for clips, retention policies for index.
- Customer preference: no PHI, but legal requires audit logs and option to run in their VPC for sensitive content.
- Action items: gather sample dataset (10 hours) + metadata TSV, confirm expected peak queries/day, confirm clip export workflow and desired clip formats (mp4 720p?).

Proposed pilot scope (MVP):
1) Discovery & onboarding (week 0–1)
   - Workshop with editorial to define search intents, sample prompt templates for summarization, and evaluation rubric (precision@k, summary ROUGE-like heuristics + editorial review).
   - Customer provides sample 10–50 hours and metadata.
2) Ingest pipeline (week 1–3)
   - Transcode (if needed) to derive audio or accept existing files.
   - ASR pass: run Redwood-hosted ASR (or integrate customer's vendor transcripts) with speaker diarization option (configurable).
   - Segmenting: scene detection (time-based + heuristics) to produce chunks for embedding.
   - Indexing: embed chunks (512–4096 token window depending on transcript density) and store in vector DB (hosted cluster for pilot).
3) Retrieval + summarization (week 3–5)
   - Retrieval chain: hybrid keyword + semantic rerank to return top-N segments with timecodes.
   - Summarization chain: LLM chain that produces 3 outputs: short (one-liner), medium (3–5 bullets), and scene-level caption.
   - Timestamp-aware output and clip start/end metadata.
4) UI & export (week 4–6)
   - Lightweight web UI for editors: search bar, facet filters (date/guest/program), result list with playable snippet, summary view, export button to request clip.
   - Clip export: job request to pull original media and transcode trim.
5) Observability & cost analysis (week 5–6)
   - Latency/cost dashboards (token-level cost breakdown, ASR-op breakdown, per-export egress cost estimate).
   - Simple quality dashboard with editorial labels and example counterexamples.
6) Wrap and recommendations (week 6–8)
   - Final report with scaling cost model, recommendations (batching, quantization profiles, dedicated capacity thresholds, private deployment if required), and next steps for productionization.

Deliverables (pilot):
- Ingested and indexed sample archive (customer dataset).
- Search UI accessible to customer editors (demo instance).
- Summarization pipeline with 3 summary formats and timestamped snippets.
- Exportable short clips with licensing audit metadata.
- Post-pilot cost model and technical recommendations doc.

Acceptance criteria (customer demo):
- Search: Editors can find 80% of a provided ground‑truth list of 50 target clips within top 10 results.
- Summarization: Editorial score >= 3.5/5 on a 40-sample blind evaluation for medium summaries.
- Export: Clip export successful for 95% of selected snippets within pilot data.
- Performance: Median search latency < 1.2s for basic queries (demo environment), end-to-end summary generation < 6s for a single program-level summary (pilot scale).

Assumptions (call these out):
- Customer provides direct S3 credentials or signed URLs for sample content.
- Up to 250 hours total for pilot (costing assumes 200 hours).
- ASR accuracy will vary by age of audio; editorial post-editing assumed.
- For privacy/compliance needs, we can offer VPC deployment but that will push timeline + cost (see optional line item).

Pricing sketch (work-in-progress):
All pricing is indicative. Final priced SOW will replace days with firm rates and contract terms.
- Discovery workshop (2 SE + 1 PM): 3 days — $9k fixed
- Ingest pipeline engineering: 10 days — $30k
- ASR & diarization processing (cloud compute + per-minute cost): estimate $0.03/min => for 200 hours = $360
- Embedding/indexing compute + DB hosting (pilot cluster, 4 weeks): $6k
- Retrieval + Summarization model runs (pilot): $4k (token costs)
- UI integration + clip export job: 7 days — $21k
- Observability & reporting: 3 days — $9k
- Project management + contingency (15%): $11k
- Optional: Private/VPC deployment setup & security review: $18k one-time + infra runbook

Pilot subtotal (hosted option): ~$90k (ballpark, includes engineering fees + infra estimates).
Optional private onboarding increases to ~$110–125k depending on security/integration work.

Resource plan (roles):
- Solutions Engineer (Marina) — PM/lead for the pilot (30% effort across pilot)
- Applied ML engineer (Ethan) — ASR + embeddings + summarization chain (50% effort during core weeks)
- Frontend engineer (contract) — UI + clip export integration (40% effort weeks 4–6)
- SRE on-call for infra/networking (ad-hoc)

Technical notes / implementation choices: 
- ASR: prefer to use Redwood’s ASR model for speed and integration, but support ingesting customer captions. Optionally run WhisperX for low-cost baseline.
- Embeddings: use dense embeddings tuned for short conversational segments. For long-form, use sliding window with overlap.
- Vector DB: pilot uses hosted RedisVector or Pinecone (customer preference). For private deployments, recommend self-hosted Milvus in VPC.
- Model selection: candidate summarizers: Llama-3-16k quantized variant (low latency) or opt-in fine-tune on editorial style (extra time/cost).
- Caching: enable prefix caching for repeated editorial queries to save token costs.
- Data retention: index TTL configurable; default 90 days for pilot.

Risks & mitigation:
- Poor transcript quality -> provide fallback to audio-based summarization and flag low-confidence sections; editorial review built into evaluation.
- Licensing/export constraints -> require legal sign-off before exporting any clip; include audit metadata in export manifest.
- Scale cost surprise -> run synthetic load tests and provide a cost model with thresholds that recommend Dedicated capacity at X queries/day.

Open questions (to resolve before SOW finalization):
- Confirm expected steady-state QPS and peak concurrent users (editor workflows).
- Does customer require encrypted-at-rest keys managed by their KMS? If so, private deployment recommended.
- Legal: precise licensing metadata fields they need in export manifest (contract id, license window, territory).
- Clip formats and maximum clip length for exports.

Next steps (internal):
- Follow up with customer to get sample bucket + metadata TSV (owner: A. Reed).
- SEs to draft formal SOW with detailed milestones and firm daily rates (owner: Marina), target due: 2025-03-10.
- Prep demo environment: spin a 2-node pilot cluster and allocate token budget for summarization tests (owner: Ethan).
- Slack thread: #proj-broadcast-pilot — start with links and invite legal for clip/export policy discussion.

Notes to self / rough TODOs: 
- Add line-item for editorial labeling UI (manual labels feed back into quality dashboard).
- Check with infra on egress cost estimates for clip exports from eu-west-1 vs us-west-2.
- Sketch sequence diagram for ingest -> index -> retrieval -> export for final SOW appendix.

Revision history:
- 2025-02-12 created (initial workshop capture)
- 2025-02-20 added pricing sketch and acceptance criteria (Ethan)
- 2025-03-04 updated timeline and private deployment option (Marina)

-- end of draft --
